chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Fats Navarro in the trumpet section: McGhee's playing and high C
summary: McGhee sits between Caypart and Fats, plays 'McGhee Special', and Fats asks how he does it; he can't play above high C.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Did you sit next to Fats in the trumpet section?
Yeah. Well, when I got up there, they had Caypart and Fats and Big Jim...

Yeah, Arthur Caypart. I don't know whether you know him or not. Light-skinned colored fellow that played decent trumpet; nothing to brag about, but a decent trumpet. And me. So the only place I could sit would be between Caypart and Fats, because I wanted to hear Fats myself. Boy, he was so pretty, he played so pretty, I couldn't imagine a cat playing that pretty.

And anyway, Andy said, 'Come on down front,' you know. So I went down in front and I played 'McGhee's Special.' And when I did that, Fats looked at me like that. He said, 'Man, how you do that?' Ah-ha! I said, 'I don't know, I just do it, Fats. I just play.' He said, 'Man, I wish I could do that.' I said, 'Don't worry. I know how to get

you to do it -- if you really want to do it." So he said, "Yeah! Well, I could love to be able to get up there." He goes, "I can't play over high-C." And he couldn't, man. And he had tried and he tried and he tried, and here and there and there, but he couldn't... Really, he couldn't get over high-C. Every now and then he might luck out a C, but he really couldn't get nothin' happening.
What was he playing like? What kind of a style?
Oh, he had a big laser-sounding style, you know, like... What's the guy that used to be with Erskine Hawkins?
Bascomb, yeah. A big pretty sound, you know. [SINGS 8 BARS OF MELLOW BALLAD]
But he wasn't playing anything of what you would call Modern.
No, he wasn't a Modern player.
No, he hadn't heard none of that. He knew J.J., though.
Oh, right. They had played together.
Yeah, they had played together. But he didn't know anything about Dizzy; he didn't know how Dizzy was playing. And when he heard me ripplin' through the

horn, he says, "God-damn, baby, I didn't know you could do that." He said, "How do you do that?" I said, "I'll show you, Fats. There ain't nothin' to it." I said, "Well, Dizzy can do that. He ripples through the horn, too." So he said, "Well, I got to learn how to do that." I said, "Yeah, if you're going to be a helluva trumpet player, you got to do that." So I said, "You want to be good, don't you?" He said, "Well, Maggie, if you say so."
